newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Analysts bullish on Manila water bid winners.
newsitem.headline: Analysts bullish on Manila water bid winners.

text.p: Ayala Corp and Benpres Holdings Corp, two local companies in consortiums which won 25-year contracts to operate and develop Manila's water system, will reap long-term benefits, analysts said on Thursday.

Ayala, in a consortium with Bechtel Corp of the United States and United Utilities, won the east zone concession, which includes most of the city's financial district, Makati. The Ayala group owns most of Makati.
The consortium has offered to charge consumers a basic average tariff rate of 2.32 pesos per litre, or 26.3886 percent of the existing average tariff rate of 8.78 pesos per litre.
Benpres, together with France's Lyonnaise des Eaux SA, won the west zone concession with a proposed tariff bid of 4.97 pesos per litre, or 56.5922 percent of the current tariff.
"They's all buys," said Gina Roa-Dipaling, assistant vice president of Philippine Asia Equity Securities. "These two have the capability to finance these two big projects."
Conrad Andres, research head of DBP-Daiwa Securities, said he considered the companies as buys in the second half of the year when cash starts flowing in from the projects.
The government has said it will turn over the concession to the two groups of winners by May.

"I'd rather sell on news and re-position later as an investment strategy," Andres said, adding he would favour banks at the current time since they will be forming a consortium to raise funds for the two projects.
Officials at the government's Metropolitan Water and Sewerage system (MWSS) have said they expect the winning bidders to invest $ 7.0 billion over the contract period to upgrade the utility.

"It doesn't pay to react quickly to this kind of thing. The stock play should a long-term one because the benefits of this deal will also be a long time in coming," said Noel Reyes, research head of Anscor-Hagedorn Securities.
Trading in shares of companies involved in the bidding was suspended on Thursday and will resume on Friday.

Ayala's bid had aimed to really win, observers said. Its bid of 2.32 pesos per litre in the east zone was half of the other bids. The next best bid had been given by a consortium led by Aboitiz Equity Ventures which was at 5.52 pesos.

"This is going to be very economically viable over the lifetime of the project," said Antonino Aquino, a senior official of the Ayala group of companies, in spite of the low price the group will charge.
He said the key would be to reduce the portion of non-revenue water, caused by leaks or pilferages, which is currently estimated at 58 percent.
Benpres Holdings said the water project would ensure that the company maintains net profit growth at an annual 25 percent.
"We have made a bid on what is bankable from our point of view," said J. Xavier Gonzales, the firm's chief operating officer.
